decisions.mark: identifies that layered build options resolve through FIVE named precedence tiers, rather than a single override
concludes that the rule is ASYMMETRIC — the stated tiers REPLACE one another while the discovered layers ACCUMULATE and survive whatever anyone states
states that tiers 3 and 4 combine IDENTICALLY, so the distinction between them is deliberately inert, and that the load-bearing line is fact-versus-guess
identifies `.clew.yaml` as the repository's own standing declaration — tier 2, discovered from the repo root by BOTH entry points rather than plumbed per section
states that tier 1 is reachable from BOTH entry points — a CLI flag and a structured options argument — so an embedding caller with no shell can still state the top tier
notes that the option names an embedding caller states are the SAME WORDS as the declaration file's section names, and the same words the diagnostics use

identifies that an unknown SECTION is refused by name against the allowed set rather than ignored, and gives the reason — an ignored section builds with defaults while reporting the declaration was honoured
identifies a SECOND refusal one level down — an unknown key INSIDE a well-named section — and that a correctly-spelled derived key is refused with its reason rather than as unknown
states that the winning tier is RECORDED with the index, and that the record is derived from the stored rows rather than stamped as a separate summary
